App.name: Learn
App.description: Short lessons on the faith, drawn from named kitabs. Available now: Qur'anic Arabic, word by word, with a real imam's recitation.

Hub.heading: Learn
Hub.intro: Learn your faith a little at a time, with simple explanations drawn from named kitabs.
Hub.tracks_heading: Choose what you would like to learn
Hub.quran_body: Listen to the imam, then understand each word: its meaning, its root, and why its ending is read the way it is.
Hub.concepts_body: A nahwu and sharaf library: each concept is explained once, then reused in every lesson that contains it.
Hub.concepts_available: {n, plural, one {# nahwu or sharaf concept} other {# nahwu and sharaf concepts}}

Quran.title: Qur'anic Arabic & Tafsir
Quran.intro: Listen to the imam, then learn each word's meaning, its root, and why it ends in fathah, dammah or kasrah. Explained simply, sourced from named kitabs.
Quran.next_body: After Al-Fatihah and Al-Mu'awwidhat: Al-'Asr, Al-Kawthar and An-Nasr.
Quran.how_1: Pick an ayah. The imam recites it, then a guided lesson explains each word, step by step. You can pause at any time.
Quran.how_2: Read each word's card: its meaning and why its ending is read the way it is. Tap “See this word's details” for its root.
Quran.how_3: Do the short exercises for that ayah, with no time limit. Then move on to the next ayah.
Quran.p1_body: Qur'anic verses are only ever heard from a human reciter. The AI voice only explains, in Indonesian, and never recites an ayah.
Quran.p2_body: Every meaning, i'rab note, tafsir point and hadith is quoted from a named kitab or dataset, with its reference.
Quran.p3_body: Explanations are prepared with AI help from named kitabs. This is learning material, not a fatwa: check the references, and ask a teacher when in doubt.

Footer.disclaimer: AI-assisted, not an authoritative fatwa. Explanations are drawn from named kitabs; check the references.

Credits.title: Sources & licences
Credits.intro: This module is built on the works and data below. We credit each source as its licence requires, and we do not store reciters' recordings on our servers: recitation streams directly from the provider.
Credits.streaming_note: When you play a recitation, your browser fetches the audio directly from the recording provider's servers abroad, so your IP address is visible to them.
Credits.data_versions_body: For technical checks: the version and file fingerprint (sha256) of every dataset the lesson pages use, exactly as recorded when the lessons were built.

NotFound.title: Page not found
NotFound.body: There is no page at this address in Learn. Check the address, or start from the home page.
NotFound.cta: Go to the Learn home page

Surah.draft_banner: Trial period: the word meanings, i'rab (how a word's ending changes with its role in the sentence) and notes on this page are prepared with AI help from named kitabs. This is learning material, not a fatwa. The ayah text and the imam's recitation themselves are unchanged.

Lesson.words_intro: This ayah has {n} words. Each card explains the word's meaning and why its ending is read the way it is.
Lesson.practice_intro: Short exercises for this ayah. Take your time: there is no time limit.
Lesson.structure_heading: How the ayah's sentence is built (tarkib)
Lesson.deeper_intro: Tap a title to open or close it.

Word.why: Why does it end this way?
Word.sharaf_heading: See how the word was formed (sharaf)
Word.sharaf_forms_note: Word forms (tashrif), not quotations of an ayah.
Word.why_letter: Why does it end with the letter {sign}?
Word.mahall_plain: Its position is {pos}, even though its ending stays the same.

Player.hint_tap: Tap a word to hear it
Player.heading: The imam's recitation
Player.husary_note: Al-Husary (Mu'allim) leaves gaps so you can repeat after him.
Player.failed: The recitation could not play. Check your internet connection, then press Listen to the ayah.

Exercise.score: {right} of {total} right on the first try. Repeating is the best way to remember.
Exercise.tap_instruction: Listen to the imam, then tap the word he recites.
Exercise.tap_not_yet: Not quite — listen once more, then pick another word.
Exercise.why_instruction: Choose the reason this word ends with that vowel mark.
Exercise.why_question: Why does this word end the way it does?
Exercise.sort_instruction: Put each word in the group for its ending. A word's ending changes with its place in the sentence (i'rab); a mabnī word keeps the same ending.
Exercise.sort_pick_first: Pick a word first, then tap its group.
Exercise.role_instruction: Choose each word's role in this ayah's sentence.
Exercise.role_question: What is this word's role in the sentence?
Exercise.wazn_instruction: One root gives several word forms. Pick the form that matches its name.
Exercise.wazn_note: These are Arabic word forms from tashrif (how a word changes form), not quotations of an ayah.

Concept.index_intro: Each concept is explained once here, then reused in every ayah and surah where it appears.

Lexeme.lemma_caption: Headword (lemma) as listed in the Quranic Arabic Corpus

Guided.title: Guided lesson
Guided.start_hint: Tap once to start — after that the lesson runs by itself.
Guided.blocked: The browser needs one more tap before sound can play. Tap “Resume”.
Guided.recite_failed: The recitation could not play. Check your internet connection, then tap “Resume”.
Guided.end_text: This is the last ayah of the surah. You can repeat it at any time.
Guided.pace_hint_biasa: Each explanation stays long enough to read, then moves on by itself.
Guided.pace_hint_pelan: Explanations stay longer, and the imam recites each word twice.
Guided.pace_hint_tunggu: The lesson stops after each explanation. Tap Continue whenever you are ready.
Guided.note_captions: The spoken explanations are being prepared; for now the explanations are shown as text.
Guided.note_imam: The ayah is always recited by the imam.

Settings.panel_body: All text grows, Arabic included. Your choice is saved on this device.
Settings.hint_title: Text hard to read? Make it bigger here.
Settings.hint_body: Pick the size you find most comfortable to read. You can change it again at any time with the “Aa Text size” button at the top of the page.
